new_results: In K_{A,B}+pq, all cross edges whose A endpoint is outside {p,q} are pairwise contained in a C7.
A robust version holds over a dense bipartite core under explicit minimum-degree hypotheses.
The natural low-cross-endpoint / near-two-clique dichotomy is refuted by an exact star-swap construction.
A fan lemma supplies m(m-2) pairwise C7-compatible edges in that construction, exposing a necessary third stability mechanism.
The first BCM Case-1 failure for k=3 is exactly the negative extension length 1-ell(P1) when ell(P1) is 2 or 3.
The top-level exact-threshold instance being in Case 2 does not bypass Case 1 under BCM's all-e strong induction.
first_unfixable_breakpoint: Prove the BCM Case-1 C7 conflict-graph chromatic lower bound, or find a replacement edge family of the required asymptotic size; the near-bipartite model lemma does not address this.
route_killed: Both the assertion that top-level Case 2 alone closes the problem and the natural low-cross-endpoint implies near-two-cliques dichotomy.
next_decidable_action: For Case 1, attack pairs whose Lemma-3.1 connecting distance is 2 or 3. For stability, prove a robust trichotomy accommodating high common cross degree, concentrated internal fans, and genuine internal density.

timing.accounting: single-agent foreground allocation; actual time only

claim_guard: Neither the local model lemma nor the unpublished Case-2 stability assertion proves Erdős #809.
